requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
**Judgment: true.** The implementation covers every obligation, and the tests cover the main cases and failure paths. I found one minor marking question, noted below.

**Implementation**
- **Location and file naming.**
  - `UsageLog::start` (src/authoring/usage.rs) creates `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`, one file per assessment. The run id is time, pid and a sequence number, and the file is opened with `create_new`.
  - The state root comes from `config::state_root`, which is marked as implementing `state_location`. It handles `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA`.
  - Both the single-run path (`author_evidence_with_output`) and the batch path (`prepare_assessment`) go through `usage_state_root` and `UsageLog::start`.
- **Record fields.** `UsageRecord` carries `version`, `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject` (the full name), `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `start_time_ms`, `end_time_ms`, `outcome`, `determination`, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written`.
  - `configured_record` fills in backend, model and subject kind as soon as they are known.
  - `assess` stores `judgment.kind()`, which is only `"true"`, `"false"` or `"FIXME"`. FIXME entry text is never stored.
  - `author_evidence_with_output` sets `evidence_output` to `file` or `stdout`.
- **Writing evidence.**
  - `configured_assessment` sets `evidence_written = true` and saves only after a successful file or stdout write.
  - `PendingAssessment::persisted` does the same in batch mode after `write_record` succeeds.
  - A failed write leaves the flag false, and the accepted determination is still kept. This is tested in `failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage`.
- **Outside the project.** `usage_state_root` and `resolved_location` resolve symlinks in the nearest existing ancestor. They refuse a state root inside the project before creating any directory, in both stdout and file modes.
- **Run status.**
  - A record starts as `outcome: "unfinished"` with no end time, and it is saved immediately.
  - `finish` sets `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled` (Ctrl-C or interruption maps to `cancelled`) and an end time.
  - A killed process therefore leaves a visible `unfinished` record.
- **State failures.** Errors from creating or writing the state location are reported without claiming the history was recorded. Error messages from `author_evidence_with_output` and `persisted` include "cannot record usage at …".
- **No content stored.** The record holds only counts, sizes, tool names and token counts. `tool_name` maps unknown tool names to `"unknown"` so model text cannot leak.
- **Marking.** The code that implements the requirement carries `{impl}` markers. The only `{cite}`-only item is the `UsageLog` struct, which is a plain holder for the record and path with no behaviour of its own. I did not treat that as a gap.

**Tests**
- **Record identity** (`usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported`):
  - The file is named `<run_id>.json`.
  - Version, project root, subject, subject kind, backend, model and `evidence_output` are correct.
  - Start time is no later than end time.
  - A blocked or undeterminable state root fails before any request, with no stdout and no evidence written.
- **Project containment** (`usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it`): both file and stdout modes are covered, and no directory is created.
- **Stdout mode** (`stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files`): true, false and FIXME each give the right kind, `evidence_output` is `stdout`, and `evidence_written` is true.
- **Failure cases:**
  - Invalid or missing submissions give `failed` with `evidence_written` false and a null determination, in both output modes.
  - Denied reads give `failed` records.
  - The failed-write case is covered.
  - The unit test `cancelled_request_persists_elapsed_time_and_incomplete_totals` covers `unfinished` and `cancelled`.
- **Content-free records:**
  - `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts that the requirement text, definition text, source payload, rationale, credential and the FIXME text `#125` are absent from the record.
  - The unit tests do the same for source text and model-supplied tool names.
- **Batch mode** (tests/authoring_batch.rs): one record per assessment, completed and failed counts, `evidence_written`, and end times on all records, including under denied reads and interruption.
- **Provider coverage:** the Bedrock CLI test and the live Bedrock test also check usage records.

:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
